cases.name: single-value-applies
cases.covers: The simplest batch. One effect, one write, one changed widget.

cases.name: writing-the-same-value-is-unchanged
cases.covers: Written once then written again. The second is a no-op, and reporting it as applied would bump the version for a script that changed nothing.

cases.name: a-later-effect-sees-the-earlier-one
cases.covers: Ordered, not batched. The second effect writes the value the first already wrote, so it can only be unchanged if the applier re-read between them.

cases.name: a-rejection-does-not-stop-the-batch
cases.covers: Preflight refused the first and nothing was written for it, so the second still runs. Only a failed write stops a batch.

cases.name: an-unknown-field-is-rejected
cases.covers: Resolution happens in preflight, so a missing field never reaches a write.

cases.name: a-toggle-state-no-widget-offers-is-rejected
cases.covers: Validated against the widgets rather than left to the engine: a state nobody offers would be written and then read back as nothing.

cases.name: a-choice-outside-the-options-is-rejected
cases.covers: A list box holds only its own options; anything else is unreachable through the widget.

cases.name: a-repeated-choice-value-is-rejected
cases.covers: Duplicates would select one option twice, which /V cannot represent.

cases.name: a-combo-box-takes-one-value
cases.covers: More than one is refused rather than truncated. Both values here ARE options, so the refusal can only come from the count: a pair of non-options would be caught by the membership check first and prove nothing about this one.

cases.name: an-editable-combo-box-takes-free-text
cases.covers: The one case where a value outside the options is legal, because the widget can type it.

cases.name: a-single-select-list-box-takes-one-value
cases.covers: The list box in this fixture is multi-select, so its two-value write is accepted. The pair here names real options, which is what separates the count rule from the membership rule.

cases.name: reset-applies-when-the-value-differs-from-the-default
cases.covers: The fixture ships this field holding a value that is not its /DV, so a plain reset has work to do.

cases.name: resetting-twice-is-unchanged-the-second-time
cases.covers: The no-op case for a reset, reached by resetting first: the value now equals the default and there is nothing to put back.

cases.name: reset-takes-several-fields-at-once
cases.covers: A reset button names a list, which is why this effect is the only plural one.

cases.name: a-push-button-cannot-be-reset
cases.covers: It has no value to go back to, and the refusal names the family.

cases.name: reset-with-no-fields-is-rejected
cases.covers: An empty list is a caller assembling a request wrong rather than a reset of nothing.

cases.name: display-changes-the-widgets
cases.covers: Judged entirely by which widgets the engine redrew, because the value is untouched and there is nothing else to compare.

cases.name: display-applies-to-every-family
cases.covers: Flags live on widgets, which every family has, so no family refuses this.

cases.name: appearance-text-leaves-the-value-alone
cases.covers: The whole point of the effect: the widget shows the formatted string and /V still holds the raw one, so the next calculation reads a number rather than a currency symbol.

cases.name: appearance-text-does-not-apply-to-a-list-box
cases.covers: Refused in preflight; only text and combo widgets have a drawable single line.

cases.name: a-radio-switch-reports-both-widgets
cases.covers: One write, two changed widgets: the one turning on and the one turning off. A caller redrawing only what changed needs both.

cases.name: an-all-no-op-batch-produces-no-meta
cases.covers: Nothing was written, so there is no artifact, no event and no version bump. This is the common outcome for a recompute-everything script: one effect the field already satisfies, one the document cannot satisfy at all.

cases.name: a-no-op-in-the-middle-does-not-stop-the-batch
cases.covers: Only a FAILED write stops a batch. Unchanged and rejected both let the rest run, which is what keeps a recompute-everything script from being truncated by its own no-ops.
